revision_rule.note: A one-line comment extends through the newline, so block-comment markers within it remain comment text.
The one-line-comment delimiter and newline termination rule makes intervening block-comment markers part of the line comment.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no string-literal line-continuation construct or the corresponding backslash-before-newline guarantee.
The same result follows from the 2017 line-continuation rule together with the 5.9.1 escape mapping of double backslash to one string backslash.
The 2017 rule states in 5.6.2 that a keyword preceded by an escape is not interpreted as a keyword.
IEEE 1800-2012 does not contain the built-in-method implicit-variable exception requiring otherwise-empty parentheses.
IEEE 1800-2017 does not specify the later exception requiring parentheses when a built-in method call is used as an implicit variable.
IEEE 1800-2012 does not state the later guarantee that every n-bit integer literal has type logic with range [n-1:0].
IEEE 1800-2017 does not define an integer literal constant as an n-bit logic vector with range [n-1:0].
The same prohibition follows from keywords being predefined nonescaped identifiers and escaped keyword spellings not being interpreted as keywords.
The 2017 keyword-versus-user-identifier distinction is stated in the keyword subclause rather than 5.6.
The 2017 quoted-string delimiter, escape-character, and physical-line rules impose the same exclusions for unescaped string content.
IEEE 1800-2012 does not provide the later universal guarantee that standard SystemVerilog system tasks consume no simulation time.
IEEE 1800-2017 does not guarantee that every standard SystemVerilog system task consumes no simulation time.
IEEE 1800-2012 ignores a backslash-newline pair in its ordinary string literal, but it has no triple-quoted string construct to which the rule also applies.
IEEE 1800-2017 ignores backslash-newline in ordinary quoted strings, but it has no triple-quoted string construct to which the rule also applies.
IEEE 1800-2012 defines the named and numeric escapes in Table 5-1 but does not define the later general backslash-followed-by-any-ASCII-character escape production.
IEEE 1800-2017 defines the named and numeric escapes in Table 5-1 but does not admit the later general backslash-plus-any-ASCII-character production.
IEEE 1800-2012 defines only the single-pair double-quoted string form; triple-double-quote delimiters are absent.
IEEE 1800-2017 supports string literals delimited by one pair of double quotes but does not define triple-double-quote delimiters.
IEEE 1800-2012 provides the optional argument-list and data-type alternatives but not the later expression/optional-expression/optional-clocking-event system-call alternative.
IEEE 1800-2012 has no triple-quoted string literal construct or its direct-newline/direct-quote content rules.
IEEE 1800-2017 has no triple-quoted string literal construct or corresponding direct-newline and direct-double-quote content rules.
IEEE 1800-2012 does not guarantee that an unrecognized string escape discards its backslash and yields the following character.
IEEE 1800-2017 does not guarantee that an unrecognized backslash escape discards the backslash and yields the following character.
IEEE 1800-2012 requires an unsized number to be at least 32 bits but does not add the later minimum-width-to-represent-the-value guarantee for values requiring more than 32 bits.
IEEE 1800-2017 requires unsized numbers to be at least 32 bits but does not add the later minimum-width guarantee for values requiring more than 32 bits, including a signed value's sign bit.
